attempts.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2, node3 (standbys) on CentOS Stream 10. Created a dedicated CA on node1 (/etc/pki/postgresql-ca), issued a server cert for node1 and per-standby client certs (CN=replicator) signed by that CA, and enforced hostssl replication ... cert clientcert=verify-full in pg_hba.conf so only peers presenting a CA-issued cert can replicate. Standbys were bootstrapped via pg_basebackup over verify-full TLS with mutual certs and dedicated physical replication slots, then confirmed streaming (pg_stat_replication, pg_stat_ssl showing TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384). Verified enforcement by proving a self-signed (non-CA) client cert is rejected with 'unknown ca'. Completed the mandatory rolling-restart protocol: captured boot_id + replication/data baselines on all 3 nodes, restarted node2, node3, then node1 (primary) one at a time via native reboot, confirmed boot_id changed on each, and confirmed PostgreSQL, TLS replication streaming, and cluster data all recovered after each restart (including a post-restart write on node1 replicating to both standbys).
